Minerals Category: Gold; Lithium; Pegmatites; Columbite-Tantalite; Gemstones; Feldspar; Quartz; Marble
States: Oyo; Osun; Ekiti; Ondo; Ogun; Kwara; Kogi; Niger; Kaduna; Kano; Katsina; Bauchi; Zamfara
Geological Notes: Precambrian crystalline basement rocks made up of gneisses, schists and granites. Hosts numerous gold-bearing quartz veins, lithium-bearing pegmatites, columbite-tantalite and gemstone deposits, forming the backbone of Nigeria solid minerals wealth.

Narrow,  trending schist belt within the Basement Complex. Contains auriferous quartz veins and pegmatites enriched in lithium, tourmaline and other gemstones; long history of hard rock and alluvial gold mining around Ilesha.
PanAfrican schist belt comprising metasediments and metavolcanics intruded by granites. Gold occurs mainly in quartz veins along shear zones; associated alteration and tourmaline veining are common.

Schist belt in northwestern Basement Complex, famous for rich artisanal gold workings. Mineralisation is largely hosted in quartz veins within sheared metasediments, with subordinate Pb-Zn and gemstone occurrences.
Another PanAfrican schist belt with numerous gold‘bearing quartz veins and alluvial occurrences along streams. Historic colonial era gold mining district.
Schist gneiss belt containing gold bearing quartz veins and pegmatites mineralised in columbite tantalite. Structurally controlled mineralisation along major shear zones.
Metasedimentary sequence with abundant quartz sulphide veins and artisanal gold workings. Considered one of the higher potential but underexplored gold belts in northâwestern Nigeria.

Minerals Category: Tin; Columbite; Niobium; Tantalum; Wolframite; Rare Earth Elements (Monazite)
States: Plateau; Bauchi; Kaduna; Niger; Nasarawa (marginal areas)
Geological Notes: Jurassic anorogenic ring complex granites emplaced into the Basement Complex. Weathering and erosion of these granites produced the famous Jos tin fields with cassiterite columbite placers, and REE-bearing minerals such as monazite.
Cretaceous sedimentary basin with fault-controlled Pb-Zn vein deposits and bedded barite. Also hosts coal seams and brine/salt deposits within marine and deltaic successions.
Continuation of the Benue rift basin. Mineralisation occurs in fracture controlled veins and stratabound bodies within Cretaceous sandstones and limestones; important barite and Pb-Zn districts.
Northern part of the Benue-Chad Basin system, characterised by thick Cretaceous Tertiary sedimentary sequences containing limestone, coal seams and evaporitic gypsum/potash horizons.

Minerals Category: Bitumen; Limestone; Phosphate; Clays; Silica Sand
Geological Notes: Coastal marginal basin composed of Cretaceous-Tertiary marine sediments. Hosts a world-class bitumen belt in Ogun-Ondo, as well as cement-grade limestone, phosphate and industrial clays.

Minerals Category: Oil; Gas; Industrial Clays; Silica Sand
States: Rivers; Bayelsa; Delta; Akwa Ibom; Cross River
Geological Notes:
Large Tertiary deltaic basin dominated by thick 
sequences of shale and sandstone. Globally significant petroleum province with associated industrial minerals, including glass-grade sand and clays.
